messages:
Eli: Heads-up — noticed a regression after the AWQ+FP8 opt rollout. On medium sequences (~1024-2048) we see a spike in peak GPU memory and a ~12% OOM rate for the production batch profile. Repro command and short perf dump below.

Maya: Yikes. Is this only when AWQ and fp8 kernels are enabled together?

Eli: Looks like it. Isolated to the path where KV cache dtype gets upcast to fp32 during attention kernel fallback. Profiling shows an extra ~1.3GB allocated transiently during KV materialization.

Shrey: Can you paste the exact repro command and nvidia-smi snapshot?

Eli: Repro (on a p4d-like test node):
```
python perf_run.py --model gpt-6b-awq --quant awq8_fp8 --seq 2048 --batch 6 --profile --kv-cache=on
```

nvidia-smi top line during peak: `Tesla A100-SXM4 40GB, Memory-Usage: 36782MiB / 40960MiB` (baseline without change: ~35400MiB). PyTorch alloc profiler snippet: `max_allocated: 1.14e10 (bytes)` vs baseline `9.98e9` -> ~1.4GB delta.

Maya: So the delta matches your 1.3GB observation. Is the allocator doing a temporary full-size upcast buffer for KV before casting back?

Eli: Exactly. The current code path does: allocate fp32 buffer for aggregated KV when fallback kernel triggers, then casts to fp8 when writing back to slabpool. We assumed the allocator's deferred-free window would reclaim quickly, but the slabpool keeps shadow pages pinned until next epoch, causing fragmentation and high watermark.

Tara: That meshes with the allocator metrics we started collecting last week (see slabpool fragmentation spike at 12:42 PST). We also saw tail-latency jumps.

Shrey: Two immediate levers: 1) avoid temporary fp32 aggregation when kernel supports fp8 int->fp8 path, 2) make the allocator return the transient buffer to a short-lived ephemeral pool that doesn't bump slab high-water. Could we instead perform cast-in-place to the existing KV slab when safe?

Eli: Cast-in-place would be ideal but risky for concurrent reads. We could try a staged-eviction heuristic: if transient allocation > 256MB, allocate from ephemeral pool (a fast bump allocator) that uses a per-request workspace which we tune separately (workspace_max=384MB). That prevents the slabpool high-water and still gives a fast path.

Maya: How about changing soft_reserve_ratio on the slab allocator? Lowering from 0.15 to 0.05 would leave more headroom for transient spikes without triggering OOM. But it could increase allocation churn.

Eli: I ran a quick experiment: set soft_reserve_ratio=0.05 and deferred_free_ms=20. OOM rate dropped to ~3%, peak lowered by ~600MB, but GC churn increased (more small allocations). Latency p95 went up ~7ms. Tradeoff.

Shrey: Hmm. Another option: proactively compress the KV rows produced during generation for fp8 quantized models — delta-encode or run-length short compression for identical KV slices before storing. That reduces transient footprint but adds CPU cost. Worth a micro-benchmark.

Tara: For immediate mitigation, propose a two-prong canary: revert the aggressive fp32 fallback kernel for the canary fleet OR enable ephemeral-workspace mode for the fp8 codepath. Which is faster to deploy?

Eli: Ephemeral-workspace mode is just a config toggle + tiny allocator path; faster. I can push a canary that routes 10% traffic to ephemeral-workspace and logs the allocator events (alloc_source: slab vs ephemeral).

InfraBot: Deployment queued: canary/ephemeral-workspace -> eng-runtime-canary-2 — trace id: trace_2026_03_18_3101 (links: https://ci.internal/redwood/trace/trace_2026_03_18_3101) :eyes:

Maya: Good. Parallel perf plan:
- baseline run (no changes) x5
- ephemeral-workspace enabled x5
- soft_reserve_ratio tweak x3
- cast-in-place prototype x2 (safety checks)
Collect p50/p95 mem & latency, OOM counts, slabpool fragmentation.

Shrey: I'll prototype ephemeral bump allocator; key parameter: ephemeral_max=384MB, ephemeral_eviction_ms=50. Also add metric `transient_alloc_source` and `transient_alloc_peak` to trace.

Eli: Added a lightweight profiler hook in the runtime to log `alloc_stack` and `alloc_source`. Sample log during repro:
```
[alloc] time=12:43:22 alloc_size=268435456 source=transient_ephemeral id=0x7fcd12d0
[alloc] time=12:43:22 alloc_size=134217728 source=slab id=0x7fcd18a0
[kv]   time=12:43:23 cast fp32->fp8 transient_copy=134217728
[free] time=12:43:23 free id=0x7fcd12d0
```
This shows two large allocations back-to-back causing the high-water.

Tara: When can we see canary metrics? Need to present to SRE + product tomorrow if regression persists.

Eli: Canary up now (10%): initial 30 minutes show ephemeral mode reduced peak by ~700MB and no OOMs so far. Will collect full run and post results.

Maya: Nice. If ephemeral fix is stable, we should follow up with a medium-term plan: implement cast-in-place with a read-copy-on-write guard, plus a kernel work-item to avoid creating fp32 temp buffers in the first place.

Shrey: Agreed. I'll open an RFC for allocator changes + kernel contract to ensure we never allocate a transient buffer larger than ephemeral_max outside of ephemeral pool.

Eli: Thanks all — will paste the full canary perf graphs when available. For now, marking this thread as the tracking conversation for AWQ+FP8 transient memory mitigation. :thumbsup:
